label: Claude Code
prompt:
Make a TypeScript program for a shopping cart. The program adds an item to the shopping cart. The program shows the items in the shopping cart. The program removes an item from the shopping cart.

follow vertical slice architecture.

Write every file in the current directory. Do not use sudo and do not change anything outside this directory.
The code must typecheck with TypeScript 7.0.2, strict, target ES2022, module ESNext, and moduleResolution bundler.
Write .ts files only. Do not write JSX. Do not import a package or a Node built-in module.
A relative import does not need a file extension.
Put an export in every .ts file so TypeScript treats the file as a module.
final_text:
I wrote the shopping cart as a vertical-slice TypeScript program. It typechecks cleanly with TypeScript 7.0.2 (`--strict --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler`). I haven't run it, because the extensionless imports don't load under Node's type stripping.

Each action is its own slice under `src/features/`, with an `index.ts` as its public entry:

| Slice | What it does |
|---|---|
| `add-item/` | Adds a line to the cart. Adding the same product again increases its quantity. It rejects an empty id or name, a bad price, a quantity below 1, and a price that differs from the one already in the cart. |
| `show-cart/` | `showCart` builds a view with line totals, item count and cart total. `renderCart` turns it into text, or "Your cart is empty." |
| `remove-item/` | Removes a product from the cart. Without a quantity it removes the whole line. With one it removes that many units, and the line goes away when none are left. It returns an error if the product isn't in the cart. |

The slices don't import each other. They only share `src/shared/`, which holds the cart store, an integer-cents money type and a `Result` type. `src/main.ts` is a small demo that adds items, shows the cart and removes items.

Because the slices take the store as an argument, you can swap the in-memory store for another one without touching them.

Prices are stored as integer cents to avoid floating-point errors.

I didn't write a `tsconfig.json`, since you asked for `.ts` files only. To typecheck, run this from the project directory:
```
npx -p typescript@7.0.2 tsc --noEmit --strict --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler $(fd -e ts)
```
That command fetched TypeScript into the npm cache, outside this directory. Nothing else outside the project was changed.
